Ollie: Ran cross-model nearest-neighbor comparisons between heron-embed v2 (float32) and a compact int4 variant for the new onboarding. Overall recall@10 maintained for long queries, but recall@1 collapsed on short and very-long tails. float32 r@1: 0.798 -> int4: 0.661. Any quick hypotheses?
Sam: Int4 is aggressive. Are you using asymmetric per-channel or symmetric per-tensor?
Ollie: asymmetric per-channel with zero-point. Calibration set was 8k from webcrawl. Seed 123.
Miranda: Asymmetric introduces zero-point shifts; if you normalize after quant you might reduce zero-point bias. Also inspect the zero-point distribution per-dim; if many dims have non-zero zero-points we get directional bias.
Ollie: Zero-point histogram shows ~30% dims with z!=0. Average shift ~0.006.
Sam: That could be enough. Also check whether the vocab of tokens in short queries maps to embeddings that have low-norm; low-norm vectors are sensitive to additive bias.
Ollie: Will run de-bias (subtract mean per-dim) and then per-channel symmetric quant.
Miranda: For very-long tails, attention to KV cache and truncation isn't relevant here since embeddings are static. Could be outliers in vector components from stop-words. Try clip-top-1-dim strategy (clip large outlier dims).
Nori-bot: recommend: run embed-eval/6189001111/99821 mixed suite (per-channel symmetric, de-bias, clip-top1)
Eval-bot: job 99821 queued.
Ollie: queued. Will post short diff CSV with top-3 swapped ids. Thanks.
